Global logistics giant DSV has opened a new 853,000-square-foot logistics facility in Laredo, Texas, the company announced on October 21 — a major bet on the border city as the strategic gateway for North American trade between the United States and Mexico.

The state-of-the-art, multi-client facility combines warehousing, transportation, customs brokerage, fulfillment, inventory management, and distribution services under one roof, DSV said in its announcement. The company says the site is designed to help businesses streamline cross-border operations while improving speed, visibility, and overall supply chain performance.

Why Laredo, why now

Laredo sits on one of the most critical trade corridors between the United States and Mexico, and it is already the busiest inland port on the U.S.-Mexico border. DSV’s announcement frames the new facility as “a milestone in DSV’s strategy to lead with innovation and scale,” in the words of Josh Summers, CEO of Contract Logistics, North America. “We’re committed to helping our customers grow by providing smarter, more agile logistics solutions,” Summers said.

“The opening of our Laredo facility represents a significant commitment to the future of North American logistics,” said Thomas Christensen, Managing Director and COO of Air & Sea for the United States. “As supply chains become increasingly complex, customers need a trusted partner capable of providing seamless transportation, warehousing, customs clearance, and fulfillment services. Our new Laredo operation delivers exactly that.”

What to watch

Every major logistics expansion in Laredo is also a test of the city’s infrastructure: roads, truck traffic, customs staffing, and the people who do the work. An 853,000-square-foot facility means real jobs — and real questions about wages, working conditions, and how much of the trade boom’s value stays in Webb County versus passing through it. Webb Watch will keep asking who benefits as the port’s growth continues. Readers should treat the company’s announcement for what it is — DSV’s own account of its investment — and judge the results by what shows up in Laredo paychecks, not press releases.
